---
title: "Test zero-length fig-cap"
format: html
---

## Figure with nonempty caption

```{r}
#| fig-cap: !expr caption
caption <- "hello world"
knitr::include_graphics("http://arfer.net/mlp/img/rara-jiggs.png")
```

## Figure with empty caption (zero-length)

```{r}
#| fig-cap: !expr caption
caption <- character(0)
knitr::include_graphics("http://arfer.net/mlp/img/rara-jiggs.png")
```
1.explanation: Quarto uses the value of the fig-cap expression to decide whether to include the figure. When the expression returns a length-1 character vector (e.g. "hello world"), the image is rendered with that caption. But when the expression returns character(0), Quarto treats the chunk as having no figure metadata and omits the image entirely. This minimal .qmd demonstrates the bug by comparing a nonempty caption chunk (which renders) against an empty caption chunk (which disappears).
1.bug_scenario: In Quarto documents using R code chunks, setting the fig-cap option via an expression that evaluates to a zero-length character vector causes the entire figure to be dropped from the rendered output. In the example below, the first chunk (with a nonempty caption) correctly renders the image with its caption, but the second chunk (where caption <- character(0)) yields no figure at all.
